etymology: English: the motion that discharges a bill from the committee that is holding it.
effect: Pulls a bill out of a committee that will not move it, using a majority that has to sign its name.
available_to: A majority of the House - 218 signatures - and a bill that a chair has decided to bury.
counter: Keep the signatures public and the bill moving. A petition is expensive to sign and cheap to schedule, so the cheapest counter is a hearing.

confused_with.tell: Cloture ends a debate in the chamber that is having it; a discharge petition takes the bill away from the chamber that is not.

senses: The House's escape hatch: when a committee refuses to report a bill, a majority of the whole House can sign a petition to bring it to the floor - 218 names, filed with the clerk, open for anyone to read.

It works because the signature is public and the alternative is invisible. A chair can kill a bill in private; a discharge petition makes every member choose in the open, which is why it is used rarely and threatened constantly.
example: *"The bill sat in committee for a year, the **discharge petition** reached 218 on a Tuesday, and the chair scheduled a hearing by Thursday."*
